newsitem.title: CHINA: British defence staff chief meets China top brass.
newsitem.headline: British defence staff chief meets China top brass.

text.p: Britain's chief of the defence staff has held talks in Beijing with Chinese counterparts in the latest sign of improving Sino-British military relations, Chinese state media said on Tuesday.

Field Marshall Sir Peter Inge was the most senior British military visitor to Beijing since military ties chilled after the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) crushed student protests for democracy in the capital in 1989, a Beijing-based diplomat said.
Inge, who has served in the British colony of Hong Kong which returns to Beijing rule in mid-1997, met PLA Chief of the General Staff Fu Quanyou on Monday, the official People's Daily newspaper said.
"We are happy to see that, under new historical circumstances, Sino-British military relations have been restored in recent years," the newspaper quoted Fu as saying.
Inge's visit to China was an event of major significance that would be the starting point for the development of friendly ties, he said.
During the talks Fu accepted an invitation from Inge to visit Britain, the People's Daily said but gave no details.

Sino-British relations have long been strained by disputes over the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997, but both sides have in recent months shown a willingness to put differences over the colony aside in an effort to boost ties.

Inge's four-day visit is the latest in a series of military contacts between Western nations and China that have signalled the waning of foreign disapproval since the PLA's suppression of the 1989 protests centred on Beijing's Tiananmen Square.
British and U.S. warships have docked at Chinese ports, and U.S. Assistant Defence Secretary Joseph Nye visited Beijing earlier this month for meetings aimed at easing battered cross-Pacific ties.
